## Summary

**BSR** (Branch to Sub Routine): Push PC to stack & program continues at label.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `SP – 4 → SP ; PC → (SP) ; PC + dn → PC` |
| Syntax | `BSR.S+ <label>` |
| Short | Push PC to stack & program continues at label. |
| Description | Pushes the long-word address of the instruction immediately following the BSR instruction onto the system stack. The program execution continues at location (PC) + displacement. The displacement is always even. For short it can appear as odd, then it extends the range by 2. This extended size is named “b2” “s2” or “s+” |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–8 | `01100001` |
| 1 | 7 | (empty in the original) |
| 1 | 6–1 | Short Extended Displacement |
| 1 | 0 | `1` |

- Range bra.s : –128 .. +126
- Range bra.s+: –256 .. –132 & 128 .. 254
- Instruction displacement byte → Real displacement word.
- 0xxx xxx1 → 0000 0000 1xxx xxx0
- 1xxx xxx1 → 1111 1111 0xxx xxx0

### Notes

- Variant on bsr.s
- Offset -130 can not be short, $ff conflict with bsr.l

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have BSR. This page covers only the 68080 addition: the .S+ short form with an odd displacement byte that doubles the short range. For the classic forms, the Motorola manual applies.

## Do / Don't

- No rules beyond the details above.
